title: U.S. House · Tennessee's 6th District
area: Middle and Upper Middle Tennessee, under the congressional map Tennessee redrew in May 2026. Incumbent Rep. John Rose did not seek re-election to this seat.

context.text: Tennessee redrew its congressional district boundaries in May 2026 (mid-decade redistricting); the filing deadline for U.S. House seats was reopened until May 15, 2026 after the new map was signed into law.
Incumbent Rep. John Rose (R) is not on the ballot for this seat; Ballotpedia's candidate list for the district shows no incumbent running in the 2026 general election.

Johnny Garrett, a state representative, won the Republican primary in a four-candidate field, defeating Van Hilleary, a former U.S. representative (TN-4, 1995–2003) and former chief of staff to U.S. Rep. John Rose, 43.4% to 29.9%.
Mike Croley won the Democratic primary with 29.0% of the vote in a five-candidate field.

candidates.name: Mike Croley
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 6 Democratic primary with 29.0% of the vote in a five-candidate field

summary.text: Mike Croley is a Navy veteran and former federal employee who worked as a Presidential Management Fellow at NOAA on climate resilience efforts before that program was ended. He is the Democratic nominee for the open 6th District seat.

background.text: Served as a Navy officer and later as a Tennessee State Park Ranger.
Worked as a federal environmental engineer and Presidential Management Fellow at NOAA, and across the Department of State, National Ocean Service, and U.S. Department of Agriculture.

priorities.text: Says he is running because he watched the federal government "get gutted by billionaires and cowards" and wants to fight for working families, teachers, and veterans.
priorities.quote: I watched the government I worked for get gutted by billionaires and cowards. I'm not a polished politician, I'm a problem solver.

priorities.text: Campaign platform: protect the environment, legalize marijuana, raise teacher pay, and invest in rural infrastructure.
Says he will fight for fair wages and access to healthcare.

candidates.name: Johnny Garrett
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 6 Republican primary, defeating Van Hilleary, 43.4% to 29.9%

summary.text: Johnny Garrett is a Tennessee state representative for District 45 since 2018 and an attorney. He is the Republican nominee for the open 6th District seat after defeating Van Hilleary in the primary.

background.text: Holds a bachelor's degree in general studies from the University of Tennessee at Knoxville and a law degree from the Nashville School of Law.
Worked as an attorney representing individuals and small- and medium-sized businesses.
Elected to the Tennessee House of Representatives, District 45, in 2018.

priorities.text: Said he supports President Trump's agenda: "I'll stand with President Trump to finish the wall, deport all illegal immigrants, cut our taxes, and stop China from buying up our land."
priorities.quote: I'll stand with President Trump to finish the wall, deport all illegal immigrants, cut our taxes, and stop China from buying up our land.

priorities.text: Ran on his state legislative record, saying he "banned biological men from women's sports, combatted illegal immigration, and defended the unborn and led the charge to back law enforcement."
priorities.quote: I've already taken on the woke left in Nashville and won as your state representative; banned biological men from women's sports, combatted illegal immigration, and defended the unborn and led the charge to back law enforcement, our first responders, and balance our budget.

positions.summary: Campaign ad states he supports finishing the border wall and deporting undocumented immigrants.
positions.quote: I'll stand with President Trump to finish the wall, deport all illegal immigrants, cut our taxes, and stop China from buying up our land.

record.text: As a Tennessee state representative, says he helped pass legislation restricting transgender participation in women's school sports.

candidates.name: Christopher Monday

summary.text: Christopher Monday is an independent candidate on the November 3 general-election ballot for Tennessee's 6th District. He was born on a Naval base in Charleston, South Carolina and has cerebral palsy.

background.text: Has cerebral palsy; graduated high school with honors.

priorities.text: Says his campaign focuses on defending individual liberties and taking the oath of office seriously.

candidates.researchNotes: Only a short Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey excerpt was found; no campaign website located.

candidates.name: Angus Purdy

summary.text: Angus Purdy is an independent candidate on the November 3 general-election ballot for Tennessee's 6th District. Ballotpedia lists no biography or Candidate Connection survey response for him.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website, biography, or public statements found for Angus Purdy beyond his name appearing on the ballot.
